subChunks.title: Adding Rows — INSERT INTO
subChunks.hookHtml: Querying data is only half the story. INSERT INTO is how new records enter the archive — and the details matter more than beginners expect.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Basic INSERT

-- Listing columns explicitly (always preferred):
INSERT INTO apprentices (name, rank, xp)
VALUES ('Helena', 'Novice', 0);

-- Omitting column list (fragile — breaks on schema changes):
INSERT INTO apprentices VALUES (7, 'Helena', 'Novice', 0, NULL);

Always list the columns explicitly. If the schema gains or reorders a column, the second form breaks silently or wrongly.

Inserting multiple rows

INSERT INTO apprentices (name, rank, xp)
VALUES
  ('Helena', 'Novice', 0),
  ('Isak',   'Novice', 0),
  ('Jana',   'Apprentice', 750);

INSERT ... SELECT

-- Copy rows from another table:
INSERT INTO archive_apprentices (name, rank, xp)
SELECT name, rank, xp FROM apprentices WHERE rank = 'Novice';

INSERT OR IGNORE / ON CONFLICT

-- SQLite — skip on unique violation:
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO apprentices (id, name, rank, xp)
VALUES (1, 'Alice', 'Apprentice', 1200);

-- PostgreSQL — upsert:
INSERT INTO apprentices (id, name, rank, xp)
VALUES (1, 'Alice', 'Apprentice', 1300)
ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET xp = EXCLUDED.xp;

storyBeats.text: Helena arrives at the Academy gates. Her first record must be inscribed in the apprentices ledger.

storyBeats.speaker: Cipher the Archivist
storyBeats.text: Always name the columns in your INSERT. Schemas change — new columns appear, columns move — and if you rely on positional order, your INSERT silently writes the wrong value to the wrong column. Explicit column lists survive schema evolution.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
🪄 New arrival

Insert a new apprentice: name 'Helena', rank 'Novice', xp 0. Use the explicit column list form. Then verify with a SELECT.

guidedPracticeTests.label: Helena row exists after insert
guidedPracticeTests.setup: CREATE TABLE apprentices (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, rank TEXT NOT NULL, xp INTEGER NOT NULL); INSERT INTO apprentices VALUES (1,'Alice','Apprentice',1200),(2,'Bjorn','Adept',2400);
guidedPracticeTests.overrideQuery: INSERT INTO apprentices (name, rank, xp) VALUES ('Helena', 'Novice', 0); SELECT * FROM apprentices WHERE name = 'Helena';

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml:
🏹 Solo

Insert three new apprentices in a single INSERT statement: Isak (Novice, 0), Jana (Apprentice, 800), Karl (Adept, 2100). Then SELECT all of them.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain why listing column names explicitly in INSERT is better than relying on column order, and describe how INSERT...SELECT works.

questions.prompt: What does `INSERT INTO t (col1, col2) VALUES (a, b)` do?
options: Adds one new row to table t with col1=a and col2=b
Appends to a list inside col1
Creates a new column named a
questions.answer: Adds one new row to table t with col1=a and col2=b
questions.explanation: INSERT INTO adds new rows. The column list maps each value to the corresponding column. Columns not listed receive their DEFAULT value or NULL if no default is defined.

questions.prompt: A table has columns (id, name, rank, xp, mentor_id). What happens if you INSERT without specifying mentor_id?
options: mentor_id receives its DEFAULT value (NULL if no default is defined)
questions.answer: mentor_id receives its DEFAULT value (NULL if no default is defined)
questions.explanation: Omitted columns receive their declared DEFAULT. If no DEFAULT is declared, the column receives NULL (which is rejected if the column is NOT NULL).

questions.prompt: What does `INSERT INTO archive SELECT name, xp FROM apprentices WHERE rank = 'Novice'` do?
options: Copies all Novice apprentice name and xp values into the archive table as new rows
Moves rows from apprentices to archive (deleting from apprentices)
Throws an error — INSERT and SELECT cannot be combined
questions.answer: Copies all Novice apprentice name and xp values into the archive table as new rows
questions.explanation: INSERT...SELECT inserts the result of a SELECT as new rows. It does not delete the source rows — it is a copy, not a move.

questions.prompt: Why is `INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 'Alice', 'Apprentice', 1200, NULL)` fragile?
options: If a new column is added to the table or columns are reordered, values map to the wrong columns or the INSERT breaks
VALUES without column names causes a syntax error
NULL values are not allowed in positional inserts
The engine cannot determine which column is the primary key
questions.answer: If a new column is added to the table or columns are reordered, values map to the wrong columns or the INSERT breaks
questions.explanation: Without column names, VALUES are mapped by position. Add a column between rank and xp and the xp value silently maps to the new column. Always list columns explicitly so the INSERT is resilient to schema changes.
